issues.reason: "rare" is named in Striking & relational generics as a KindProperty-class property that no single instance can hold, so the conclusion (Member $x rare) hands every fever-causing bite a property the instruction set says an individual cannot have — false content, and the very distribution KindProperty exists to prevent.

Both stated relative-clause templates (the donkey rule and "everyone who owns a dog is a pet owner") put a plain event variable in the premise; a Skolem-function term belongs only to a conclusion's per-binding event, so (Member (sk_cause $x) cause) as a premise can never match an ordinary event witness and the rule is inert.

gaps_confirmed: a clausal restriction in ConditionalProperty's condition slot — the slot is specified for adjectives/states, measures/environments and locative or domain PPs, not for a relative clause
adversative "though" between two clauses that reify no eventualities: no endpoints, so the contrast has no carrier
repair_summary: Replaced the distributing Implication with (ConditionalProperty spider_bite rare cause_fever) — the route the instruction set gives for a kind-level claim narrowed by a restriction ("voles are common in the fens", explicitly extended to KindProperty-class properties, with "never strip the restriction") — and added the compound-action decomposition (Inheritance cause_fever cause) + (Patient cause_fever fever), mirroring the parse's own cause_death treatment.
notes: Putting a compound action rather than a state in the condition slot is the gap above, but it keeps the restriction and asserts nothing of individuals; the seeded cond_prop caveat for non-distributing properties is already registered in the instruction set and does not change what is emitted. Sentence 2's atoms were correct and are untouched.
